problem: "more than 50% of power" leaves the unit of power undefined; students on a proof-of-work chain read hash power, on a proof-of-stake chain the same sentence is wrong unless stake is named.
fix: "if colluding miners control more than 50% of the hash power (or validators more than 50% of the stake), they can rewrite recent history."

problem: The lead promises a cost for every feature but lists only six costs (collusion risk, lost privacy, lower throughput, fees, key loss, oracle trust) for seven features; the auditability limit (bad input stays bad) is missing from the list.
fix: Add the missing cost, e.g. "... fees, key loss, oracle trust or unverified input."

problem: "51% collusion can rewrite recent history, not the entire chain" is too absolute: the standard limit is that a majority attacker can reverse their own recent transactions and block new ones, but cannot spend other users' coins or change block rewards; depth is limited in practice by cost and checkpoints, not by the protocol.
fix: "Tamper-evident is not tamper-proof; majority collusion can reverse recent transactions and block new ones, though it cannot spend other users' coins or change block rewards."

problem: The node labelled "Final" with note "forks possible" appears only in the figure; the myth list in Section 3 never discusses finality, so the caption's claim that each branch carries a limit explained in the text does not hold for that branch.
fix: Either delete the "Final" node or add a myth line in Section 3: "Final. A confirmed block can still be reorged; finality is probabilistic or reached by checkpoints, not instantly."

problem: The central "Claims" node carries the note "5 pools", which describes the worked example, not the idea of a claim; a reader can mistake the centre for a pool count.
fix: Change the centre note to something like "claims and their limits", and keep "45% pool" on the Unhackable node.
